Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women Article 46 ie

To anticipate and prevent acts of violence against Women from occurring, the Regional Government shall undertake the following efforts: a. b. f. g providing various public facilities that are appropriate for Women in public spaces; developing an integrated information system database on acts of violence against Women,; strengthening the competence of apparatus handling violence against Women; making various modules and guidelines on the prevention and handling of acts of violence against Women,; conducting various trainings and guidance for social workers working in organizations/institutions handling violence against Women,; inviting the community to play an active role in recovery and reintegration; strengthening the function of community organizations working in the field of Women's empowerment; conducting various socializations regarding the prevention and anticipation of acts of violence against Women to various components of society in the Region; and optimizing the role of religious institutions, customary institutions, culture, as well as exploring local wisdom in order to prevent and minimize violence against Women occurring either at home or outside the home.

Article 44

The Regional Government in its efforts to protect Women as referred to in Article 42 is responsible for doing the following:

a. planning, making, establishing and organizing policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women; strengthening and developing institutions providing Women's protection services,; taking various preventive measures early so that violence against Women does not occur or can be minimized; massively and continuously making various efforts to prevent acts of violence against Women in all areas of life; massively and continuously preventing TPPO from occurring; and
f. continuously striving to protect Women workers.

Article 198

Every parent whose home has a Woman, has a role in the following matters:

a. provide equal and comparable opportunities to Women in terms of obtaining access and opportunities to pursue education at all levels; prevent every Woman who is part of the family members under their leadership from receiving arbitrary, harsh, and inhumane treatment; protect female family members from pressure and sexual harassment, physical and psychological violence that causes the Woman concerned to be unable to live her life properly; prevent a female family member from entering into early marriage below the age limit determined by the Law; and not force a female family member to marry a man whom she does not desire.

Article 10

Every Woman has the following rights:

a. b. f. to live in prosperous conditions physically and mentally; to live in a family in a lawful marriage bond in accordance with the teachings of the religion adhered to; to obtain education and teaching in all types, levels and pathways of education; to obtain protection from acts of discrimination; to obtain protection from economic and sexual exploitation; to obtain protection from physical, psychological, sexual violence, and neglect; to obtain decent work based on ability, interest and talent while upholding all matters related to her humanity; to obtain access in advancing the business undertaken in order to create adequate income improvement; to obtain work leave while receiving wages/income in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; to obtain special protection in the performance of work or profession against matters that may threaten safety and/or health in relation to Women's reproductive function, k. to obtain legal information and services in accordance with her needs; to enjoy a good and healthy environment in accordance with standards and provisions of laws and regulations; to own and manage joint property in a lawful marriage in accordance with laws and regulations; and to have other rights attached in accordance with her human dignity based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 4

The purpose and objectives of this Regional Regulation are as the basis and guidelines for the Regional Government and stakeholders to:
a. fulfill the rights of Women and Children; b. protect Women and Children maximally, provide a sense of security and peace for Women and Children; c. prevent violence against Women and Children; d. empower Women; e. empower Women victims of violence; f. provide services to Women and Children victims of acts of violence; g. provide protection to Reporters and Witnesses; h. maintain the integrity of the household so as to realize a harmonious family; i. encourage the realization of quality families; and
j. k. increased participation of non-governmental institutions to support Regional efforts in providing protection for Women. Article 5

The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. obligations and Responsibilities of the Regional Government; b. rights of Women and Children; c. improvement of the quality of life of Women in the Region; d. protection of Women; e. family quality; f. fulfillment of Children's rights; g. special protection for Children; h. i. Gender and Child Data System; j. k. funding; l. participation of Parents, Family/Relatives and/or the Community; m. monitoring and Evaluation; n. guidance and Supervision; and

m. prohibitions and sanctions.

Article 58

In handling complaints as referred to in Article 54 letter a, Regional Apparatus as referred to in Article 55 is given authority to handle victims of acts of violence against Women obtained through other information.

Article 52

Protection of Women victims of violence shall be implemented through the provision of integrated services.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Women are humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently Vv after they have recovered and been provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 Year 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with the family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and

Hy participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32. Children with Disabilities are Children who have physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 33. Children with Excellence are Children who have commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or have potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guarding for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence will, is or has occurred to victims. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in suffering or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences suffering and/or suffering that occurs in the area of Pekanbaru City. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who are already infected with HIV both at the stage where there are no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of written instructions that are standardized regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it must be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. Article 2

Protection of Women is carried out with the following principles:
a. respect and appreciation for Human Rights; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. empowerment; e. best interests for women; Vv f. protection; g. continuity and sustainability; h. openness; i. order; j. legal certainty; and
k. local wisdom. Article 3

Protection of Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and appreciation for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. best interests for the Child; d. respect for the Child's opinion; e. the right to life, grow, and develop of the Child; and
f. local wisdom.

Article 56

Complaints of acts of violence against Women may be made by complainants consisting of: victims; family; community; and/or community organizations engaged in the field of Women's protection.

Article 26

Curative efforts as referred to in Article 23 letter are implemented by means of:

a. b. optimizing technical service units related to complaints of violence against Women; providing adequate facilities and infrastructure for handling health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid; and conducting handling of victims of crime and violence quickly, precisely, and accurately by law enforcement officials.

Article 102

The strengthening and development of women's protection service provider institutions as referred to in Article 101 is intended so that cases of violence against Women can be handled with:

a. accurate targeting;
b. innovation; and
c. professional handling, by skilled personnel who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pekanbaru City. 2. Regional Government is the Pekanbaru City Government. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 7. Head of the Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Children, or father and his Children, or mother and her Children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to the difference in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the administration of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that are gender responsive and child sensitive. 15. Disaggregated Data is data selected by sex and age. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 19.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Head of the Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Children, or father and his Children, or mother and her Children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to the difference in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the administration of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that are gender responsive and child sensitive. 15. Disaggregated Data is data selected by sex and age. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 19.

Article 4

The purpose and objectives of this Regional Regulation are as the basis and guidelines for the Regional Government and stakeholders to:
a. fulfill the rights of Women and Children; b. protect Women and Children maximally, provide a sense of security and peace for Women and Children; c. prevent violence against Women and Children; d. empower Women; e. empower Women victims of violence; f. provide services to Women and Children victims of acts of violence; g. provide protection to Reporters and Witnesses; h. maintain the integrity of the household so as to realize a harmonious family; i. encourage the realization of quality families; and
j. k. increased participation of non-governmental institutions to support Regional efforts in providing protection for Women. Article 5

The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. obligations and Responsibilities of the Regional Government; b. rights of Women and Children; c. improvement of the quality of life of Women in the Region; d. protection of Women; e. family quality; f. fulfillment of Children's rights; g. special protection for Children; h. i. Gender and Child Data System; j. k. funding; l. participation of Parents, Family/Relatives and/or the Community; m. monitoring and Evaluation; n. guidance and Supervision; and

m. prohibitions and sanctions.

Article 179

Special Protection for Children victims of sexual crimes as referred to in Article 167 letter is carried out through efforts:

a. b. education on reproductive health, religious values, and moral values; social rehabilitation; psychosocial assistance during treatment until recovery; and provision of protection and assistance at every level of examination from investigation, prosecution, to examination in court proceedings.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with the family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and

Hy participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32. Children with Excellence are Children who have commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or have potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guarding for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence will, is or has occurred to victims. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in suffering or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences suffering and/or suffering that occurs in the area of Pekanbaru City. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who are already infected with HIV both at the stage where there are no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of written instructions that are standardized regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it must be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. Article 2

Protection of Women is carried out with the following principles:
a. respect and appreciation for Human Rights; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. empowerment; e. best interests for women; Vv f. protection; g. continuity and sustainability; h. openness; i. order; j. legal certainty; and
k. local wisdom. Article 3

f. local wisdom.

Article 10

Every Woman has the following rights:

a. b. f. to live in prosperous conditions physically and mentally; to live in a family in a lawful marriage bond in accordance with the teachings of the religion adhered to; to obtain education and teaching in all types, levels and pathways of education; to obtain protection from acts of discrimination; to obtain protection from economic and sexual exploitation; to obtain protection from physical, psychological, sexual violence, and neglect; to obtain decent work based on ability, interest and talent while upholding all matters related to her humanity; to obtain access in advancing the business undertaken in order to create adequate income improvement; to obtain work leave while receiving wages/income in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; to obtain special protection in the performance of work or profession against matters that may threaten safety and/or health in relation to Women's reproductive function, k. to obtain legal information and services in accordance with her needs; to enjoy a good and healthy environment in accordance with standards and provisions of laws and regulations; to own and manage joint property in a lawful marriage in accordance with laws and regulations; and to have other rights attached in accordance with her human dignity based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 44

The Regional Government in its efforts to protect Women as referred to in Article 42 is responsible for doing the following:

a. planning, making, establishing and organizing policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women; strengthening and developing institutions providing Women's protection services,; taking various preventive measures early so that violence against Women does not occur or can be minimized; massively and continuously making various efforts to prevent acts of violence against Women in all areas of life; massively and continuously preventing TPPO from occurring; and
f. continuously striving to protect Women workers.

To Establish A REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pekanbaru City. 2. Regional Government is the Pekanbaru City Government. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pekanbaru City. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Office is the Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties and functions of the affairs of

Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 7. Head of the Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Children, or father and his Children, or mother and her Children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to the difference in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the administration of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that are gender responsive and child sensitive. 15. Disaggregated Data is data selected by sex and age. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 19.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Women are humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently Vv after they have recovered and been provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 Year 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with the family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and

Hy participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32. Children with Disabilities are Children who have physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 33. Children with Excellence are Children who have commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or have potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guarding for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence will, is or has occurred to victims. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in suffering or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences suffering and/or suffering that occurs in the area of Pekanbaru City. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who are already infected with HIV both at the stage where there are no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of written instructions that are standardized regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it must be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. Article 2

Protection of Women is carried out with the following principles:
a. respect and appreciation for Human Rights; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. empowerment; e. best interests for women; Vv f. protection; g. continuity and sustainability; h. openness; i. order; j. legal certainty; and
k. local wisdom. Article 3

Protection of Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and appreciation for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. best interests for the Child; d. respect for the Child's opinion; e. the right to life, grow, and develop of the Child; and
f. local wisdom.

Article 24

Promotive efforts as referred to in Article 23 letter are implemented by means of:

a. strengthening coordination mechanisms and working networks between service units in handling violence cases; wv providing Communication, Information, and Education (IEC) materials related to the prevention and handling of violence; and conducting socialization, advocacy and social campaigns in the context of prevention and handling of violence.

Article 166

Implementation of special protection of Children is conducted through: a. b. prevention of violence against Children; provision of services for Children requiring special protection through coordination of parties from government and non-government institutions in the Region; and strengthening and development of service provider institutions for Children requiring special protection.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women Article 46 ie

To anticipate and prevent acts of violence against Women from occurring, the Regional Government shall undertake the following efforts: a. b. f. g providing various public facilities that are appropriate for Women in public spaces; developing an integrated information system database on acts of violence against Women,; strengthening the competence of apparatus handling violence against Women; making various modules and guidelines on the prevention and handling of acts of violence against Women,; conducting various trainings and guidance for social workers working in organizations/institutions handling violence against Women,; inviting the community to play an active role in recovery and reintegration; strengthening the function of community organizations working in the field of Women's empowerment; conducting various socializations regarding the prevention and anticipation of acts of violence against Women to various components of society in the Region; and optimizing the role of religious institutions, customary institutions, culture, as well as exploring local wisdom in order to prevent and minimize violence against Women occurring either at home or outside the home.

Article 44

The Regional Government in its efforts to protect Women as referred to in Article 42 is responsible for doing the following:

a. planning, making, establishing and organizing policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women; strengthening and developing institutions providing Women's protection services,; taking various preventive measures early so that violence against Women does not occur or can be minimized; massively and continuously making various efforts to prevent acts of violence against Women in all areas of life; massively and continuously preventing TPPO from occurring; and
f. continuously striving to protect Women workers.

Article 171

Special Protection for Children in conflict with the law as referred to in Article 167 letter is conducted through: ir a. f. g.

k. 1, humane treatment with attention to needs according to their age; separation from adults; provision of legal aid and other assistance effectively; application of recreational activities; freedom from torture, punishment or other treatment that is cruel, inhumane and degrades dignity and worth; avoidance of imposition of the death penalty and/or life imprisonment; avoidance of detention or imprisonment, except as a last resort for the shortest period of time; provision of justice before a Children's court that is objective, impartial, and in a hearing closed to the public; avoidance of publication of their identity; provision of assistance from Parents/Guardians and persons trusted by the Child; provision of social advocacy; provision of private life; provision of accessibility, especially for Children with Disabilities; provision of education; provision of health services; and provision of other rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

j. k. increased participation of non-governmental institutions to support Regional efforts in providing protection for Women. Article 5

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pekanbaru City. 2. Regional Government is the Pekanbaru City Government. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pekanbaru City. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Office is the Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties and functions of the affairs of

Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 7. Head of the Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of Pekanbaru City or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Children, or father and his Children, or mother and her Children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to the difference in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the administration of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that are gender responsive and child sensitive. 15. Disaggregated Data is data selected by sex and age. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 19.

Provision of services for Children requiring special protection as referred to in Article 166 letter is carried out through:

a. implementation of service provision for Children requiring special protection through Regional Apparatus carrying out Governmental Affairs in the field of Women's empowerment and Child protection in the Region; provision of public complaint services for Children requiring special protection in the Region; provision of outreach services for Children requiring special protection in the Region; provision of case management services for Children requiring special protection in the Region; provision of temporary shelter services for Children requiring special protection in the Region; f. provision of mediation services for Children requiring special protection in the Region;
g. provision of assistance services for Children requiring special protection in the Region; and h. provision of service facilities and infrastructure for Children requiring special protection in the Region.

Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Women are humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently Vv after they have recovered and been provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 Year 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with the family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and

Hy participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32. Children with Disabilities are Children who have physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 33. Children with Excellence are Children who have commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or have potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guarding for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence will, is or has occurred to victims. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in suffering or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences suffering and/or suffering that occurs in the area of Pekanbaru City. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who are already infected with HIV both at the stage where there are no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of written instructions that are standardized regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it must be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. Protection of Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and appreciation for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. best interests for the Child; d. respect for the Child's opinion; e. the right to life, grow, and develop of the Child; and
